But I agree with Bob that it would be better to have stan do the parallelizing.

Maybe you and Jack are missing the fact that "running
Stan" has nothing to do with ESS? Stan isn't a monolothic
all-in-one-command thing like R2WinBUGS.

You only do ESS calculations AFTER "running Stan".
If you run multiple chains in parallel,
you'll have multiple chains to put into ESS.

That's how I built the system-call R interface and
presumably what Jiqiang's doing in the real RStan.

- Bob

I don't thing gtest does, at least not by default. But if you do

make -j8 test-unit

then make will use 8 threads to compile and run the unit tests. However, g++ uses much more RAM than clang++, so it may not actually be feasible to utilize g++ with 8 threads on the unit tests.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: parallelization
parts:
There are two options for parallelization.

The easier route is just to run in several processes,
each in a single thread. The data gets copied for each
chain and there may be a bit of I/O contention depending
on the size of the output and buffering to disk. This
would include using a cluster to run on several machines.

The harder route is to get serious about making
Stan run in multi-threaded mode. The code's there now,
but it hasn't been tested cross platform and there's
not an easy way to turn multithreading on/off (with it
on, the autodif slows down by about 15% due to thread
contention for the thread-local auto-dif stacks.

- Bob
